conversation_log.content:
To begin, how would you best describe your history in competitive sport?
Options: [I've spent years competing in organized, high-level sports. | I’ve always been active and athletic, but usually in a recreational or individual capacity. | I'm looking to pivot into a new high-performance discipline as a fresh challenge.]
I've spent years competing in organized, high-level sports.

As you consider your next high-performance chapter, which physical dimension feels most aligned with your natural strengths and ambitions?
Options: [Explosive power and high-velocity speed | Extreme, long-haul endurance and mental grit | Technical precision and complex tactical mastery]
Technical precision and complex tactical mastery

As you look toward this next phase of your sporting journey, how do you see your role in the arena?
Options: [I thrive in high-stakes team environments, relying on coordination and collective strategy. | I prefer the solitary, meditative pursuit of mastering a specific craft or technical discipline. | I am drawn to the bridge between strategy and execution, such as coaching or designing training systems.]
I thrive in high-stakes team environments, relying on coordination and collective strategy.

scouting_result.scout_verdict:
At 165cm and 60kg, you possess a center of gravity and density that make you a natural force in the high-intensity theater of wrestling. Your preference for tactical mastery and team-driven strategy means you won't just be an individual athlete on the mat; you will be the anchor for your training block, treating every bout like a complex puzzle where you outmaneuver your opponent through sheer technical calculation. As you build toward The LA28 Games, your previous experience in high-level competition will serve as your compass, allowing you to read the flow of the match with the maturity of a veteran leader.

In your adaptive pathway, you step into the world of powerlifting, where tactical mastery takes the form of internal physics and precise kinetic output. Competing in the -67kg category, your focus shifts to the disciplined science of lift optimization, weight class management, and explosive force production. Here, the 'team' aspect is essential—you are part of a squad of lifters who calibrate every repetition and micro-adjustment to reach peak performance. It is a sport of absolute precision, where your ability to analyze your own bio-mechanics under load will redefine what you believe your body is capable of achieving.

scouting_result.pathway_adaptive: Para-Alpine Skiing (e.g., Women's Super-G Sit-Ski LW12)
scouting_result.scout_verdict:
This pathway pivots your focus from close-quarters combat to the razor-thin margins of high-velocity technical precision. Whether carving lines on a mountain slope or finding the rhythm on the speed skating track, you are testing the absolute limits of momentum and edge control. Your background in high-stakes, team-oriented sports will be your greatest asset as you enter the relay and squad-based training environments leading up to The Brisbane 2032 Games, where collective strategy is the difference between a podium finish and the pack.

Your adaptive pathway brings you to Para-Alpine Skiing under the LW12 classification—a category for athletes with lower-limb impairments who compete using a sit-ski. Mastering this discipline is the ultimate test of technical command; it requires an intimate, tactical connection between your core, the chair’s balance, and the snow beneath your edges. Because LW12 requires such a high level of postural and equipment control, your focus on 'technical mastery' becomes the primary variable of your success. You aren't just sliding; you are navigating the mountain through a complex technical dialogue between human, equipment, and environment, all while supported by the strategic coordination of a highly specialized racing team.
